title: Why root cannot rewrite ro properties
hook: Why does `setprop` on a `ro.` property fail, and who really owns property_service?

scenes.caption: An existing ro. property cannot be overwritten with setprop.
scenes.narration: On a disposable development device, read the build fingerprint, then attempt to replace it. Setprop fails; the exact error text depends on your Android build.

elements.text:
adb shell getprop ro.build.fingerprint
adb shell setprop \
  ro.build.fingerprint debug
# Expected: setprop reports failure

items: Root does not make it writable

scenes.caption: setprop requests a change from init's property service.
scenes.narration: Setprop is a client. Init owns property_service, which validates the request and updates shared property storage; changing a shell environment variable never changes it.

items: Read access uses shared property data
Write requests cross a policy boundary

scenes.caption: Permission checks and write-once behavior are separate gates.
scenes.narration: The caller needs permission for the property's labeled type. Even an authorized caller cannot replace an existing read only property through the normal service.

items: SELinux controls who may set a name
ro. means write once, not root only

scenes.caption: Change the defining build or boot input, then boot the new image.
scenes.narration: For a permanent change, locate the build or boot input producing the property. Rebuild and boot the appropriate image, then verify the value again.

elements.text:
# AOSP checkout: locate producer
rg 'ro.build.fingerprint' build
# After the updated image boots:
adb shell getprop ro.build.fingerprint

items: Use a writable property for runtime state
persist. does not bypass write permissions

takeaway: ro. properties are write-once through property_service; root does not override that rule.
